definitions.meaning: Autonomous spending entering the circular flow from outside it, here $100 of government spending.
The loop of spending and income between households and firms that carries each round of re-spending.
Income that leaves the circular flow each round as saving, tax or imports, here $20 of the first $100.
The marginal propensity to consume: the fraction of each extra dollar of income that is re-spent, here four-fifths.
The ratio of the final rise in national income to the injection that caused it, here $500 / $100 = 5.
The total income generated in the economy; here it rises in shrinking rounds and settles at $500.
Total planned spending in the economy; its curve shifts right in shrinking steps as the rounds are re-spent.
Spending that does not depend on current income, such as the initial government injection.
One lap of re-spending: income received in one round is partly re-spent in the next, smaller round.

mechanismSteps: The injection enters: government spending puts $100 into firms, and it flows to households as income in the circular flow (s1).
Round 1 leaks: households spend the $100, but $20 leaks out as saving, tax and imports, so only $80 goes round again (s2).
Rounds shrink geometrically: round 2 adds $80 and round 3 adds $64, each four-fifths of the last, and the total climbs to $244 (s3).
AD settles: aggregate demand shifts right in shrinking steps until national income settles at $500, five times the injection (s4).
objectives: Describe the multiplier process: an injection is re-spent in geometrically shrinking rounds as leakages bite
Explain why national income settles at $500, five times the $100 injection, so the multiplier is 5
Use the MPC and the leakages to predict how each round shrinks
subject: economics
title: The multiplier process: one injection, shrinking rounds

trap.explanation: The slip: The injection is spent in full in the first round, so it looks as if the same full amount keeps circulating round after round. The fix: Only part of each round's income is re-spent - the rest leaks away as saving, tax and imports - so each round adds a geometrically smaller amount and national income settles at a multiple of the injection. In class, replay scene 3: freeze the bars at $100, $80, $64 and ask what each round would look like if the full injection were re-spent - every bar would stand at $100 and the total would never settle; the shrinking bars show it cannot, so each round must lose its leakage first.
trap.misconception: Every round re-spends the full injection, so national income grows by the same amount each round without limit.

workedExample: Work the multiplier from the injection. Step 1 (s2): round 1 adds $100 and $20 leaks out, leaving $80 to re-spend. Step 2 (s3): round 2 adds $80 and round 3 adds $64 - each round is four-fifths of the last. Step 3 (s4): the shrinking rounds sum to $500, five times the $100 injection, so the multiplier is 5.
